note: The harness's controls for itself. It is the instrument the rest of the catalogue is measured with, so its own load-bearing branches — is the named test really there, did the mutation really compile, did the file really come back — are proved the same way everything else is.

controls.clause: A verdict is about one named test: a parent's or a sibling's fail event does not make a passing subtest red
A mutation that does not compile proves nothing, whatever the package-level fail event says
A skipped test ran but proved nothing — the trap AGENTS.md records, that go test prints ok for a package whose tests all skipped
A mutation whose old text is absent or repeated is refused before the file is touched: zero proves nothing and two change a branch nobody named
restore re-reads the file and checks it against the recorded checksum; a mismatch is an error and never a silent success
A test that already fails goes red under any mutation, so the run stops at the baseline rather than recording it as proof
The test is run against the mutated file, not against a tree already restored
A journal written before the mutation names the file, the snapshot and the checksum, so a harness killed mid-run leaves evidence rather than a silently edited tree
Every outcome but RED is a finding: a test that cannot fail for the clause it appears to cover is what the harness exists to surface
controls.old: func (o Outcome) ok() bool { return o == Red }
controls.new: func (o Outcome) ok() bool { return true }

controls.clause: A test name is anchored element by element, so TestWrap does not also select TestWrapFence
A filter that selects no control is an error, because "0 controls, all red" is a green run reporting that nothing was proved
Every part of a control is required: AGENTS.md's rule is one control per requirement clause, and a control that cannot state its clause is a cheap mutation wearing a number
A flag after a positional filter is still a flag: Go's flag package stops at the first non-flag argument, which would read --json as a control name
